acts.desc: A couple guys show off a pretty creative invention.
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: There are young single men and women at the camps, and there’s some flirting for sure. But usually it doesn’t seem to go very far. One of our producers Sean Cole met a couple camped out at a gas station. (14 1/2 minutes)
acts.title: You Just Keep on Pushing My Love Over the Borderline

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: People don’t have a lot of money in the refugee camps, and our producer Miki Meek went to see what that’s like at a camp that’s been built on the grounds of an abandoned psychiatric hospital. About 1,300 people are living there. They’re Yazidi, a religious minority from Iraq.
acts.title: Thank You for Smoking

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: There’s a camp trying to set the gold standard for what refugee camps are to be. It’s in an actual beach vacation resort. Joanna Kakissis went there.
acts.title: Last Resort

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: One night at L-M Village, a panic-struck man walked up to Robyn Semien from our staff. He said his wife had a medical problem.
acts.title: Take Another Little Piece of My Heart

acts.label: Act Five
acts.desc: Sean hit up this one piece of coverage that wasn’t like any of the others. He got a little obsessed with it.  Follow refugees.tv on Facebook.
acts.title: Smile, You’re on Handmade Camera
